Subject: Dedicated burst / autoscale plan for Helix Systems

Hi Emma — good to speak yesterday. Quick follow-up with the next steps so we can size the Dedicated pool and draft the autoscale agreement.

Recap of what I heard on the call:
- You expect baseline inference at ~220 vCPU-equivalent requests per minute (RPS) across your two US regions, with unpredictable 10–20 minute burst events up to ~2x baseline during marketing pushes.
- P95 latency target: 350ms; p99 target: 800ms for critical latency routes.
- Regulated models must run inside your VPC Dedicated deployment; you want a non-disruptive fallback path to a smaller quantized variant for severe contention.

To move forward we need two quick confirmations from your side:
1) Confirm the acceptable burst ceiling (2x vs 3x baseline) and whether bursts may coincide across both regions.
2) Which routes are non-negotiable for p95 (e.g., search-suggest, checkout summarization) so we can prioritize routing rules.

Attached is a preliminary capacity worksheet (we'll update after your answers): [attachment: helix_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm profile + finalize matrix: 1 business day after your reply
- Redwood internal sizing + policy draft: 2 business days
- Joint review + sign-off: within a week

If helpful, we can propose two options: a) conservative shoulder-reserve (paid commit) that guarantees 2x bursts with prewarm lanes, or b) a credit-backed burst ledger (cheaper, shorter bursts covered but prioritized by weights).

Thanks — I'll loop Ben and Aditya internally to sketch the policy.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks Connor — quick answers inline.

> Confirm the acceptable burst ceiling (2x vs 3x baseline) and whether bursts may coincide across both regions.
We want to support up to 3x for short windows (<= 15 minutes) for US-east only; US-west is lower priority and can be capped at 1.5x. Cross-region simultaneous peaks are uncommon but possible.

> Which routes are non-negotiable for p95?
Search-suggest and real-time personalization are hard SLOs. Everything else can tolerate graceful degradation to 1s p95 during extreme events.

We'd be open to the credit-backed ledger approach if it means lower monthly commit. Can you include an example run-rate and overage model? Also need the SLA language around preemption and eviction notice (we have an internal ops requirement for 5 min advance preemption signals).

Marcus

Subject: Internal: draft autoscale + burst governance for Helix (proposal attached)

Connor / Monica — based on Connor's note and Marcus's clarifications, here's a compact proposal we should send to Helix. Attachment contains the capacity math.

Key recommendations:
- Per-deal reserved shoulder: 2 reserved slots (NVLink A100-equivalent) per region for warm prewarm; bill as reserved capacity to guarantee up-to-2x baseline for US-east.
- Burst credit ledger: 10,000 burst credits per month (1 credit ~= 1 minute of one reserved slot at peak config). Credits roll monthly with a 30% carryover cap.
- Short high-magnitude bursts (<= 15 min, <= 3x) consume credits first; if credits depleted, soft-throttle policy starts with:
  * p95 guardband: allow up to +10% latency above SLO for prioritized routes while shedding non-critical routes;
  * Preemptible slab fallback: non-critical workloads get routed to preemptible nodes (lower cost, eviction expected).
- Preemption / eviction notice: Redwood runtime will emit an advance signal 5 minutes before eviction and a 30s graceful drain hook — satisfies Helix ops requirement.
- Failover model variants: automatic fallback to quantized T0 variant in same region when capacity constrained (disabled by default; opt-in per route).
- Weighted routing / route-scaling: mark 'search-suggest' and 'personalization' as highest weight for queue priority; they consume fractional weight tokens to preserve QoS during smoothing.
- Cost model: we'll present two scenarios in the attachment — (A) Reserved-heavy (higher monthly commit, minimal overages), (B) Credit-ledger (lower base, higher overage unit price).

Operational runbook snippet (for SREs):
1) Alert: queued tokens > 20% capacity for 3 minutes -> prewarm shoulder slots if available.
2) If queued tokens exceed threshold after prewarm -> consume burst credits and raise 'burst-consumption' event.
3) If credits exhausted and p95 > SLO + 10% -> enable soft-throttle and route non-critical to preemptible slab.
4) Escalation: auto-page Redwood ops and Helix on-call at 10% residual capacity for 5 minutes.

Attachments: proposed-autoscale-SLA-draft.pdf, helix_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx

Emma / Marcus — looping everything together with a concrete mutual action plan. Thanks Marcus for the 3x ceiling clarity for short windows. Below is a short, signable plan (summary) and asks. Full proposal attached.

Summary of proposed plan (for sign-off):
- Reserved shoulder: 2 warm A100-equivalent slots in US-east; 1 warm slot in US-west (optional) to cover 1.5x.
- Burst ledger: 10k credits/month, 30% carryover. 3x bursts allowed up to 15 minutes in US-east; credit consumption rate is explained in the attached matrix.
- SLO routing: mark search-suggest & personalization as 'priority' (guaranteed p95 <= 350ms up to credit exhaustion).
- Preemption & eviction: Redwood will provide 5-minute advance eviction signals plus 30s drain hooks; we will log and surface these events in the Redwood Console for Helix (audit + telemetry).
- Failover: automatic fallback to quantized model variant (opt-in per route).

Next steps / asks from Helix:
1) Approve the above summary in email (reply-all) with either: \"Option A: reserved-heavy\" or \"Option B: credit-ledger\".
2) Confirm whether you want the US-west warm slot (we'll price separately).
3) Share the list of exact route names that must be marked priority in the router.

If you sign off, we'll: finalize the SLA draft, produce a one-page runbook for your SREs, and schedule a policy handoff with your ops team (30–45 minute session).

Thanks — sending the attachments now: [attachment: proposed-autoscale-SLA-draft.pdf] and the capacity matrix already included earlier.
